headline: Shift Grid Costs to Large Energy Users
short_summary: This bill aims to make large energy users, such as data centers, responsible for their own grid infrastructure costs, potentially reducing the burden on residential ratepayers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential ratepayers, consumer advocacy groups, Governor's administration.
opponents: Data center industry, large industrial energy users.
news_headline: Virginia mulls shifting major grid costs to data centers
news_summary: Virginia regulators are considering how data center developers should shoulder more of the costs for transmission projects, which are currently spread across the public. State residents have paid billions for data center-related transmission lines since 2021, prompting calls from consumer and environmental advocates to shift these costs to the industry.

headline: Mandate Data Center Water Use Reporting
short_summary: This bill requires water suppliers to report water volumes provided to data centers, enhancing transparency and aiding state environmental planning.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, local governments, water conservationists, Senator Kannan Srinivasan.
news_headline: New regulations beef up data centers' required water use reporting in Virginia
news_summary: New regulations, effective January 2027, will increase transparency on data center water usage in Virginia by requiring waterworks operators to categorize and report monthly sales data to data centers. This legislation, championed by Senator Kannan Srinivasan, aims to fill a data gap for state environmental quality and water supply planning, especially during droughts.

headline: Regulate Data Center Siting and Noise
short_summary: This bill mandates site assessments for noise impacts and allows localities to require additional impact reviews for new large data centers, empowering communities in development decisions.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residents near data centers, environmental advocates, Virginia League of Conservation Voters.
opponents: Data center developers, real estate industry.
news_headline: A Roanoke Delegate Helped Write Virginia's New Data Center Law. Here's What It Does, and What It Doesn't
news_summary: A new Virginia law, effective July 1, 2026, requires developers of the largest data centers to conduct site assessments examining noise impacts on nearby residential units and schools within 500 feet. While the law mandates studies and disclosures, it does not set specific noise limits, water caps, or setbacks, leaving some community advocates wanting more stringent regulations.
